summary.oneLiner: the near term is an invest-ahead trough.

one-line thesis: India's largest MSO delivered a solid top-line quarter (consolidated income Rs 1,020 cr, +12% YoY / +9% QoQ) but PAT collapsed to Rs 2.3 cr because it front-loaded the full cost and capitalization (higher depreciation + finance cost, ~Rs 6 cr) of its HITS "GTPL Infinity" satellite platform while the cost savings are still to flow. The strategic pivot is clear: HITS lets GTPL serve any village at a fixed transponder cost (uneconomic on P2P fibre), enabling entry into Kerala and J&K this quarter and a bolt-on of ~6 lakh subs via the Rs 36.23 cr ACT Group Digital TV acquisition (closing 15-Sep-2026). Management guides operating margin from 22% → 25% as HITS benefits materialise from Q3/Q4 — the near term is an invest-ahead trough.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Standalone: revenue Rs 693 cr (+16% YoY, +12% QoQ), subscription Rs 213 cr (+2% QoQ), EBITDA Rs 64.4 cr / 9.3% margin, PAT Rs 1.9 cr. PAT decline is the headline distortion: EBITDA fell only ~Rs 3 cr but PAT fell ~Rs 8 cr, entirely from ~Rs 6 cr higher depreciation + finance cost on capitalized right-of-use HITS assets ("conservative accounting" — full cost taken upfront, savings deferred).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Operating margin: 22% → 25% as HITS benefits materialise (lifts both EBITDA and PAT).
Capex FY27: ~Rs 400 cr, split ~50% Broadband / ~50% Digital TV.

ACT acquisition: close by 15-Sep-2026; adds ~6 lakh Digital TV subs (AP, Telangana, Odisha, Karnataka); EBITDA-accretive; full P&L effect from mid-Q2 into Q3. No revenue/EBITDA contribution figure given yet ("in the next call").
HITS benefits: ~40–50% realised this FY, 100% from next FY; full effect end-Q3 / start-Q4 FY27.
Broadband extraction (conversion) rate: 16–17% → 20–21% on the 5.95 mn home-pass base.
New markets (Kerala, J&K): 6–12 month gestation before cable-business turns positive.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (subscription model). Forward pipeline = subscriber ramp: (a) ACT ~6 lakh subs closing 15-Sep-2026; (b) Kerala (addressable 6.5–7 mn TV HH, GTPL has 75–80k base) + J&K (addressable 4.5–5 mn) organic + inorganic build-out, Broadband launch to follow; (c) HITS platform now at ~2.7 mn subs (2.5 mn converted + ~0.2 mn new). Digital TV base 9.60 mn (8.9 mn paying); >51,000 business partners; Broadband active base 1.06 mn (+10k YoY).
segment / subsidiary detail: Digital TV: 9.60 mn subs (8.9 mn paying). Revenue dipped YoY on new-market entry at lower ARPU + churn in established markets; management expects recovery as expansion scales via HITS. AP+Telangana already >1 mn subs; ACT lifts this to ~1.6–1.7 mn (market leadership).

Broadband: 1.06 mn active subs; ARPU Rs 470 (up from Rs 465, +Rs 5 YoY) driven by up-tiering to higher-speed plans; data consumption 436 GB/user/month (+6% YoY). Home pass held at 5.95 mn (~75% FTTX-ready); strategy shifting back to both extraction (16–17% → 20–21%) and renewed home-pass expansion under new CEO Vivek Raina. Gujarat focus market.
HITS (GTPL Infinity): launched FY26; ~2.7 mn subs on platform; Rs 4 cr bandwidth saving already in Q1; fixed transponder cost → serves 1 mn or 50 mn at same cost, margin rises with scale.
Combo product (Cable + Broadband + OTT/games): live and "growing very good," lifting stickiness and cross-sell; a combo pilot underway in a few cities.
growth verticals / optionality: HITS-enabled rural/greenfield expansion: 26 states + 5 UTs covered; only ~2 states / ~3 UTs left. India has ~210 mn TV HH of ~350 mn total; ~140–150 mn HH still without TV — HITS makes sub-5,000-subscriber villages economically serviceable for the first time.
Broadband under-penetration: management pegs FTTX at only ~50 mn of a very large household base — long runway; renewed home-pass investment.
M&A consolidation: ACT is a template; management signals more acquisitions and "aggressive expansion."
Cross-sell/upsell: combo bundles + up-tiering to higher-speed broadband plans.
margins & cost dynamics: Consolidated EBITDA margin 10.7% (on total income) / operating margin 22% (on operating revenue). Margin was broadly maintained despite carrying the full HITS cost load. The PAT-vs-EBITDA gap is the key: right-of-use HITS asset capitalization pushed depreciation + finance cost up ~Rs 6 cr, so PAT fell ~Rs 8 cr on only ~Rs 3 cr lower EBITDA. Bandwidth optimization keeps broadband delivery cost flat despite rising data usage. HITS structural economics: fixed cost / variable subscribers → operating leverage as base grows.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): FY27 capex ~Rs 400 cr (~50% Broadband / ~50% Digital TV). ACT acquisition Rs 36.23 cr cash, closing 15-Sep-2026. New-market build-out (Kerala, J&K) initially Digital-TV/HITS-led (low fixed cost — per-subscriber STB cost), Broadband fixed-cost investment to follow. Watch: ACT deal-close slippage past 15-Sep, and HITS benefit timing (guided end-Q3/Q4) — both are dated commitments to verify.
capital allocation: Capital directed to: HITS platform (already capitalized), FY27 capex Rs 400 cr (broadband + digital TV infra), and bolt-on M&A (ACT Rs 36.23 cr). Conservative accounting stance (full HITS cost capitalized upfront). No buyback/dividend detail on this call. Depreciation + finance costs rising as HITS and new-market assets come on stream.
risks & watch-items: PAT optics: thin PAT (Rs 2.3 cr consol) while HITS costs are carried but savings deferred — margin recovery is a forward promise (25% operating margin), unverified until Q3/Q4.
New-market gestation: Kerala & J&K need 6–12 months to breakeven; ARPU dilution and upfront discounts near term.
Digital TV revenue decline YoY: new-market lower-ARPU mix + churn; recovery is expansion-dependent.
Competitive intensity: Jio, Airtel Broadband/AirFiber, DTH, local cable operators — especially in new markets.
Content acquisition cost inflation (annual/biennial) — managed via broadcaster negotiation + selective price hikes.
ACT integration/closure risk (targeted 15-Sep-2026); contribution figures not yet disclosed.
management quality / tone: Confident and detailed on strategy, candid on the PAT miss — Piyush Pankaj proactively decomposed the ~Rs 8 cr PAT decline into depreciation/finance cost and explained the "conservative accounting" choice to front-load HITS cost. Honest that new markets need 6–12 months to turn positive and that ACT contribution figures are being withheld until the deal closes. The HITS economics were explained with a clear worked example (Chhindwara P2P-fibre cost vs satellite). Tone: long-term, expansion-focused, some promotional framing ("largest MSO," "aggressive").
non-obvious takeaways: The PAT collapse is an accounting/timing artifact, not operational — HITS cost fully capitalized upfront (depreciation + finance +~Rs 6 cr) while savings (Rs 4 cr bandwidth saving already visible) ramp over the year; management explicitly guides margin expansion once HITS matures.

HITS is the strategic unlock, not just a cost item: it removes the ~5,000-subscriber economic floor that forced GTPL to abandon small/rural markets on P2P fibre — the real reason Kerala/J&K entry and pan-India ambition are now feasible.
Broadband strategy pivoted from pure extraction back to dual extraction + home-pass expansion under a newly hired CEO — signals renewed broadband capex intent after a stable-footprint phase.
ARPU guided flat at ~Rs 470 despite rising data consumption — up-tiering offsets, but management is not banking on further ARPU-led growth near term; volume/scale is the lever.

> Other topics (HITS economics, ACT acquisition, ARPU) are firm-specific with no external listed beneficiary to map.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): Consol income Rs 1,020 cr (+12% YoY, +9% QoQ); EBITDA Rs 109 cr / 10.7%; operating EBITDA Rs 101 cr / 22%; PAT Rs 2.3 cr (−~Rs 8 cr YoY on HITS depreciation/finance cost). Standalone rev Rs 693 cr (+16%). Digital TV 9.60 mn subs (8.9 mn paying); Broadband 1.06 mn subs, ARPU Rs 470, 436 GB/user/mo. HITS ~2.7 mn subs, Rs 4 cr bandwidth saving. Entered Kerala & J&K. Signed ACT BTA (Rs 36.23 cr, ~6 lakh subs, close 15-Sep-2026). New Broadband CEO Vivek Raina. Guidance: op margin →25%, FY27 capex Rs 400 cr (50/50), extraction 20–21%, ARPU ~Rs 470, HITS 100% next FY.

Next Q → check: ACT deal closure by 15-Sep & first contribution figures; operating-margin progress toward 25%; HITS savings ramp (Q3/Q4); Broadband home-pass expansion + extraction-rate move; Kerala/J&K subscriber traction; Digital TV revenue recovery.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.
